ComPoM

ComPoM fits Poisson-multinomial models to compositional count data (e.g. length or age frequencies from observer sampling) and uses them to standardise compositions for non-representative sampling and scale them to total catch or standardise them for use with index fisheries in stock assessments.

Counts per bin and sampling stratum are modelled as Poisson with the stratum sample size as offset. All covariate effects are bin-specific, so that the implied within-stratum proportions follow a multinomial-logit model:

  • effects of interest (e.g. year) enter as bin-specific fixed effects (ffx_form);
  • nuisance sampling factors (e.g. vessel, season) enter as bin-specific IID random effects (re_form);
  • continuous covariates (e.g. sea-surface temperature) enter as smooths over covariate and bin (cvars, spl);
  • with the sdmTMB backend and a mesh, bin-specific spatial and spatio-temporal Gaussian random fields are added.

Models are fitted with brms (Bayesian) or sdmTMB (maximum likelihood). The model equations are given in vignette("ComPoM").

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("dragonfly-science/ComPoM")

Or from a local clone, in the package root:

devtools::install()

Documentation, function reference and vignettes are at https://dragonfly-science.github.io/ComPoM/.

Requirements

  • R >= 4.1.
  • The sdmTMB backend (backend = "TMB") needs sdmTMB, which compiles C++ code on installation and needs a C++ toolchain (Rtools on Windows, Xcode command line tools on macOS).
  • The brms backend (backend = "brms") fits Stan models and needs a Stan interface and a C++ toolchain. Install rstan (the default, brms_backend = "rstan") or cmdstanr (brms_backend = "cmdstanr"). See the brms and Stan installation notes.
  • The vignettes need the suggested packages (tidyverse, patchwork, sf, terra, fmesher, MASS).

Workflow

Step Function Purpose
1 data_prep() Aggregate counts to strata x bins, add zero counts and stratum totals
2 fit_model() Build the formula (via parse_form()) and fit with brms or sdmTMB
3 post_pred_group() Posterior predictive check by group (needs add_preds = TRUE)
3 Fx_plot() Bin-specific effects of a factor, as multipliers
3 cvar_smooth_plot() Smooth effect of a continuous covariate by bin
3 spatial_field_plot() Spatial field by bin (spatial sdmTMB fits)
4 scale_comps() Predict numbers-at-bin draws for strata with known catch or CPUE
4 scaled_comp_plot(), scaled_ridge_plot() Aggregate draws to compositions and plot

Models are usually developed in increasing complexity: fixed effects only, then nuisance random effects, then covariate smooths, then spatial fields.

Basic usage

The package includes simulated sampling data (ex_comp, one row per stratum and length bin) and the catch of the strata (ex_catch), see ?ex_data.

library(ComPoM)

# 1. Prepare data: one row per stratum x bin. Include every variable that is
#    used later (fixed effects, nuisance effects, covariates, coordinates).
dat <- data_prep(
  comp              = ex_comp,
  vars_for_grouping = c("Year", "Season", "Vessel", "trip"),
  bin_lab           = "length",
  count_var         = "count"
)

# 2. Fit: Year as effect of interest, Season and Vessel as nuisance effects
fit <- fit_model(
  ffx_form  = "Year",
  re_form   = "Season + Vessel",
  data      = dat,
  backend   = "TMB",     # or "brms"
  add_preds = TRUE
)

# 3. Diagnostics and effects
post_pred_group(fit, grp = "Year")
Fx_plot(fit, grp = "Year")

# 4a. Catch weighting: composition of the total catch of the fleet.
#     ex_catch has one row per stratum with its catch; all nuisance variables
#     are predicted at each stratum's level.
scaled <- scale_comps(
  scale_df = ex_catch,
  predvar  = "catch",
  fit      = fit,
  grps     = c("Year", "Season", "Vessel")
)
scaled_comp_plot(scaled, grps = "Year")

# 4b. Index population: the composition of the population that a CPUE index describes.
#     Season and Vessel are selectivity terms (random effects) and are set to the
#     population level. The grid has one row per index time step (here one per year).
scaled_pop <- scale_comps(
  fit  = fit,
  mode = "index",
  grps = "Year",
  grid = data.frame(Year = factor(2015:2020))
)
scaled_ridge_plot(scaled_pop, grps = "Year", plot_y = "Year")

With backend = "brms", fit_model() samples with Stan (chains, iter, warmup, thin control the sampling), and the draws are posterior draws. With backend = "TMB" the draws are simulated from the approximate joint distribution of the estimates (nsim = (iter - warmup) / thin), so iter, warmup and thin only set the number of draws. Check the sdmTMB fit with sdmTMB::sanity(fit$model), and see the warning raised by fit_model() when the Hessian is not positive definite.

Continuous covariate smooth

sst is a variable in ex_comp. It has to be included in vars_for_grouping, and be numeric. In scale_comps(), covariates are averaged within each stratum of scale_df, so set them to a reference value in scale_df to standardise to that value.

dat_sst <- data_prep(ex_comp, c("Year", "Season", "Vessel", "trip", "sst"), "length", "count")
dat_sst$sst <- as.numeric(as.character(dat_sst$sst))
fit_sst <- fit_model(
  ffx_form = "Year", re_form = "Season", data = dat_sst, backend = "TMB",
  cvars = "sst", spl = "by_factor", knots = "4"
)
cvar_smooth_plot(fit_sst, "sst")

Spatio-temporal model (sdmTMB backend) 

library(sdmTMB)

dat_sp <- data_prep(ex_comp, c("Year", "Season", "Vessel", "trip", "x", "y"), "length", "count")
# coordinates are factors after data_prep(); convert to numeric
dat_sp <- dplyr::mutate(dat_sp, x = as.numeric(as.character(x)), y = as.numeric(as.character(y)))
mesh <- make_mesh(dat_sp, xy_cols = c("x", "y"), cutoff = 25)

fit_sp <- fit_model(
  ffx_form = "Year",
  re_form  = "Season + Vessel",
  data     = dat_sp,
  backend  = "TMB",
  mesh     = mesh,
  time     = "Year",
  coords   = c("x", "y")
)
spatial_field_plot(fit_sp)

For spatial models, the scaling data passed to scale_comps() must contain the coordinates, and the time column must have the same class (e.g. factor) as in the model data. Spatial and spatio-temporal fields are estimated for every bin, so they need data at many locations per year. With few locations the model is not identifiable and the Hessian is not positive definite.

Vignettes

  • ComPoM: model equations (basic and spatio-temporal), workflow and a simulated example.
  • vessel_bias_simulation: correction for vessel-level sampling bias (brms and sdmTMB).
  • spatial_bias_simulation: correction for spatially biased sampling, and covariate smooths.

The vignettes are slow, because they fit models (the spatial vignette takes about 10 minutes). They are not built by R CMD check in CI. The vignettes workflow renders them, and the rendered versions are on the package website.

Testing

Tests use testthat:

devtools::test()

The tests include recovery of a known composition from simulated data and an end-to-end run of the workflow above. The brms tests are skipped if rstan is not installed.

GitHub Actions run R CMD check (Linux, macOS, Windows), test coverage with covr, the vignettes, and the pkgdown site on every push and pull request. Coverage is reported on Codecov. To compute coverage locally, run

covr::report(covr::package_coverage())
